title: Halo: an AI overlay that hears your calls and suggests what to say
status: draft 2026-10-28: selected from the 28 Oct radar; owner approved the batch of 2

facts.engine: one OpenAI-compatible client: Gemini, Groq, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio (README)
facts.speech: VAD + any whisper-compatible API, or local whisper.cpp / faster-whisper (README)
facts.rewind: Ctrl+Shift+Enter recaps 30 s to 5 min: what happened, what they need, what to say (README v2.1)
facts.scale: ~3,100 lines, 0 runtime dependencies, 27 unit tests, keys encrypted by the OS (README)
facts.rules: README disclaimer: many interviews, exams, employers and platforms prohibit outside help or recording

verify_before_render: Re-open github.com/stormydayy/halo-overlay: licence, Rewind shortcut and the disclaimer must still match the capture.
Re-read the star count from the GitHub API and update facts.stars if it moved.
If the repo is archived, removed, or the licence changes, do not render.

treatment.audience: professionals who sit in interviews, meetings and sales calls live
treatment.viewer_job: decide whether a live AI call assistant helps them, and where the line is
treatment.hook_mechanic: stakes first: an interview disqualification, then the tool that risks it

cover_concepts.gap: how does it hear both sides?

viewer.who: people who handle interviews, meetings and sales calls live and hate losing the thread
viewer.problem: in a live call you cannot pause, and once you zone out you do not know what they just asked

idea: Halo is a floating AI overlay that hears both sides of a live call, watches your screen, and suggests what to say, with a Rewind key that recaps what you missed.

claims.text: Halo is a minimal AI overlay that floats over your screen, listens to the conversation, sees the screen and gives short suggestions in the moment.
It captures two audio channels labelled Them and You, and suppresses your mic while the other side speaks.
Rewind (v2.1): Ctrl+Shift+Enter answers from the last 30 seconds to 5 minutes of transcript plus screen keyframes in three lines: what happened, what they need, what to say.
It works with any OpenAI-compatible model including local Ollama, is GPL-3.0, ~3,100 lines with 0 runtime dependencies, and API keys are encrypted by the OS.
The README itself warns that many interviews, exams, employers and platforms prohibit outside help or recording.

proof_plan.how_shown: hook camera lands on the repo title and intro while the stakes are spoken
overlay scene: camera on the Them/You audio-channels line as it is spoken
rewind scene: camera on the Rewind section and its three-line answer
catch verdict: free-and-open-source and local lines spoken
catch verdict: the rules line spoken last

scenes.heading: HALO *WHISPERS* THE ANSWERS?
scenes.say: An AI that listens to your job interview and whispers the answers sounds perfect, until it gets you disqualified.

scenes.heading: IT HEARS *BOTH SIDES*
scenes.say: This is Halo, an overlay that floats over any call. It hears both sides of the conversation, watches your screen, and suggests what to say next.

scenes.heading: ZONED OUT? *REWIND*
scenes.say: Lost the thread? Rewind answers in three lines: what happened, what they need from you, and what to say.

scenes.heading: THE *CATCH*
pros: Keys stay encrypted by your OS
scenes.say: The catch: it is free and open source, and your keys stay encrypted, but you bring your own model or run it fully local, and many interviews ban outside help.
Would you use this on a real sales call? Comment halo and I will pin the repo.
